summary: Early identification of cognitive impairment is crucial for preventing dementia progression. Magnetic resonance elastography (MRE), combined with traditional imaging markers, provides a novel dimension for cognitive assessment in cerebral small vessel disease (CSVD). title: Greater Lifetime Alcohol Consumption is Associated with Smaller Hippocampal Volumes in Adults with Low-Level Alcohol Intake.
summary: For decades, low-level alcohol consumption, operationalized as no more than two standard drink equivalents/day for males and one standard drink equivalent/day for females, was indicated to carry minimal systemic health risks. However, the neurobiological correlates of low-level drinking in healthy adults are not well characterized. To date, no study has concurrently assessed the associations of lifetime low-level alcohol consumption, modeled as a continuous rather than categorical or ordinal variables, with hippocampal volumes in healthy adults. title: Brain systems supporting the narrative self and psychopathology.
summary: Disturbances in the narrative self are implicated across psychiatric disorders, with abnormalities in the neural systems supporting its generation and regulation constituting a transdiagnostic risk factor for mental illness. This review highlights how alterations in these brain systems underlie prevalent clinical features, including diminished, rigid, and sustained negative beliefs within the narrative self. The narrative self is framed as a higher-order construct that emerges from multiple systems, with reward, punishment, and motivational signals biasing which experiences are encoded as self-defining and which self-beliefs are reinforced over time. title: EEG Feature-level integration for robust command generation in SSVEP-based brain-computer interfaces.
summary: Steady-state visual evoked potential (SSVEP)-based brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) have been widely studied for efficient command generation via spatiotemporal information integration and advanced stimulation paradigms. However, users may intentionally or unintentionally suppress SSVEP responses, leading to the SSVEP Blocking Response (SSVEP-BR). This phenomenon, characterized by attenuation or disappearance of SSVEP, has been largely overlooked despite its potential for command generation without additional stimuli. title: Acute sleep deprivation induces ECM-associated transcription and MMP12-sensitive perivascular remodeling.
summary: Sleep deprivation (SD) disrupts brain homeostasis, but whether acute sleep loss alters extracellular matrix (ECM) programs and the structural organization of the perivascular interface remains unclear. We integrated re-analysis of three public 6-h SD transcriptomic datasets with cisterna magna tracer studies, collagen IV and hyaluronan-binding protein 2 (HABP2) imaging, cellular localization of matrix metalloproteinase-12 (MMP12), transmission electron microscopy, pharmacological MMP12 inhibition, and continuous EEG/EMG recording during ZT0-ZT6 and recovery, with manual sleep-wake scoring in 4-s epochs. title: Robust joint estimation of regional brain activity and inter-regional source covariance via full-structure covariance learning.
summary: Uncovering the mechanisms underlying cognition and brain disorders requires accurate regional source imaging and reliable characterization of inter-regional statistical dependencies. Traditional methods typically follow a two-stage pipeline that first performs source imaging and then calculates inter-regional dependence measures separately. Such a decoupled framework can propagate source-reconstruction errors to covariance-based network analyses, leading to biased source localization and distorted dependency patterns. title: Association of Neighborhood Opportunity and Abdominal Obesity with Brain Development and Cognitive Function in Adolescents: A Prospective Cohort Analysis.
summary: To investigate the longitudinal associations between neighborhood opportunity and brain structure and cognitive performance among adolescents, and to explore whether these associations differ by sex, maturational status, race/ethnicity, and abdominal obesity trajectory. Prospective data from ABCD Study participants with complete baseline data (n = 9,375; ages 9-10 years, 47% girls; 21 U.S. sites), followed from 2016-2018 to 2020-2022, were analyzed; outcome-specific analytic samples were 9,121 at 2 years and 3,048 at 4 years. title: Workup of Encephalopathy in Patients Receiving Cancer Immunotherapy.
summary: Cancer immunotherapy has transformed many areas of oncologic care. Neurological immune-related adverse events, particularly encephalopathy, represent potentially life-threatening complications requiring prompt recognition and intervention. Encephalopathic syndromes occur across immunotherapy modalities, including immune checkpoint inhibitors, chimeric antigen receptor-T cell therapy, and bispecific antibodies. The diagnostic challenge lies in distinguishing immune-mediated neurotoxicity from infection, metabolic derangements, disease progression, and paraneoplastic syndromes. title: Multiscale DCE-BOLD MRI reveals vascular uncoupling patterns for IDH genotyping in adult glioma: A prospective habitat-based study.
summary: Isocitrate dehydrogenase (IDH)-wildtype gliomas exhibit heterogeneous vascular dysfunction, but whole-tumor analyses may obscure regional variation in vascular permeability and functional reserve. We developed a multiscale habitat framework integrating dynamic contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (DCE-MRI)-derived volume transfer constant (Ktrans) and resting-state blood oxygen level-dependent functional MRI (rs-BOLD-fMRI)-derived relative cerebrovascular reactivity (rCVR), including a 10-mm peritumoral margin, for noninvasive IDH genotyping. title: Wavelets and switching in bistable visual perception: Comment on "Wavelet analysis in biomedical research: A versatile tool for multiscale signal characterization and functional connectivity analysis" by Kralj et al․.
summary: This Comment highlights bistable perception as a link between wavelet-based signal characterization and functional connectivity. Prior frequency-tagged Necker-cube experiments used wavelet power to identify candidate perceptual switches and assess selective attention, while complementary EEG studies examined network organization. Integrating time-local dominance estimates with dynamic connectivity could clarify how network reconfiguration relates to switching. Such analyses require behavioral validation, consideration of wavelet resolution, and separation of connectivity from power changes. Frequency tags remain indirect perceptual markers, not intrinsic brain rhythms.

title: Processed electroencephalogram-guided anesthesia and its impact on postoperative delirium and perioperative efficiency: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
summary: Processed electroencephalography (pEEG) provides quantitative indices for monitoring anesthetic depth and is recommended in international guidelines. Prior meta-analyses have assessed EEG-guided anesthesia but none have evaluated available evidence stratified by pEEG technology. We performed a systematic literature review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials in adults undergoing surgical, endoscopic, or dental procedures comparing pEEG-guided with non-pEEG-guided anesthesia. Primary outcomes were anesthetic drug use (TIVA and volatile agents) and postoperative delirium (POD ≤10 days). title: Asymptomatic congenital CMV infection: long-term cognitive outcome and brain imaging findings.
summary: Infants with symptomatic congenital cytomegalovirus infection (cCMV) are at high risk of neurodevelopmental impairments. However, long-term cognitive outcomes in children with asymptomatic cCMV (acCMV) remain unclear. Through universal CMV screening of approximately 20,000 newborns, children with acCMV (n = 36), children with symptomatic cCMV (n = 4), and matched healthy controls (n = 54) were identified and followed prospectively. Brain MRI and neuropsychological assessments were performed in children with acCMV and controls at 6-8 years of age. title: Concordance between magnetoencephalography and intracranial EEG and association with surgical outcomes in MRI-negative epilepsy.
summary: Magnetoencephalography (MEG) is increasingly used in the presurgical evaluation of drug-resistant epilepsy (DRE), particularly in MRI-negative cases. However, the relationship between MEG localization, intracranial EEG (iEEG) concordance, underlying pathology, and surgical outcomes remains incompletely defined. We performed a retrospective cohort study of 51 patients with MRI-negative DRE who underwent MEG and iEEG evaluation at our center from 2009 to 2025. title: The inferior parietal lobule is associated with suicidal outcomes in adolescents and youths with non-suicidal self-injury.
summary: Non-suicidal self-injury (NSSI) is a leading predictor of suicidal thoughts and behaviors in adolescents and youths, yet the neurobiological mechanisms underlying this transition remain unclear. The Integrated Motivational-Volitional (IMV) model links NSSI to suicidal outcomes, but its phases have rarely informed neuroimaging work. We examined 173 adolescents and youths (117 NSSI, 56 non-NSSI) recruited from a psychiatric hospital who underwent structural MRI. title: Age-stratified neuroimaging correlates of psychiatric symptoms in first-episode schizophrenia: Insights from structural and functional MRI.
summary: To investigate changes in brain structure and function, their correlations with psychiatric symptom severity, and possible neuropathological differences in patients with first-episode schizophrenia (FES) with different ages of onset. A total of 76 patients with FES and 67 age- and sex-matched healthy controls (HCs) were enrolled. Patients with FES were stratified based on the onset age into two subgroups as follows: (i) early adult onset (EOS, 18-25 years) and (ii) young-middle-aged onset (YMOS, 26-45 years). title: Generative structure-guided denoising diffusion probabilistic model for MR to CT image synthesis in radiotherapy planning.
summary: Radiotherapy (RT) planning uses magnetic resonance (MR) imaging for soft tissue information, while computerized tomography (CT) imaging is necessary for dose calculation. Synthetic CTs generated from MR images streamline the clinical workflow by reducing the need for an actual CT acquisition while minimizing radiation exposure, enabling adaptive RT workflows. Appraoch: We propose a radiotherapy planning model combining stable structure-guided denoising diffusion probabilistic model (DDPM) with MRI conditioning, for generating synthetic CT (sCT). title: Predictive value of EEG/ECG biomarkers for treatment response in depression.
summary: Major depressive episodes frequently show limited response to first-line treatments, motivating the search for objective biomarkers. EEG/ECG-based support tools aggregating electrophysiological predictors may guide treatment selection. We examined whether antidepressant treatments concordant with an EEG/ECG-biomarker report were associated with higher response rates. We retrospectively analyzed adults with ICD-10 depressive disorder or bipolar depression treated with electroconvulsive therapy (ECT), repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS), (es)ketamine, or selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs) between 2022 and 2024. title: Early Characterization of Hypoxic-Ischemic Encephalopathy: Contribution of Biochemical, Imaging, and Electrophysiological Markers to Patient Profiling in the Ancillary Cohort LyTONEPAL.
summary: To identify and characterize different profiles of newborns with hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy (HIE) according to clinical, biochemical, electrophysiological, and brain imaging data. An analysis was conducted on the Long-Term Outcome of Neonatal hypoxic EncePhALopathy in the era of neuroprotective treatment with hypothermia ancillary cohort, including 204 newborns with mild to severe HIE. Multiple factor analysis and hierarchical ascendant classification were performed using clinical, biochemical, electrophysiological, and imaging data to establish clusters representing the cohort. title: Early movement intention recognition via corticomuscular synchrony in complex tasks.
summary: Intuitive control of assistive robots requires precise decoding of movement intention before muscle activation. While corticomuscular coherence (CMC) tracks descending corticospinal drive, decoding pre-onset intention during complex, multi-target tasks remains challenging. This study identifies stable CMC markers characterizing the transition from motor planning to execution. Twelve healthy volunteers performed target-directed reaching tasks using a 6-DoF robotic arm controlled via a wireless wearable inertial interface. title: Optimization of phase-contrast MRI shunt flow measurement across multiple scanners for the management of hydrocephalus.
summary: Ventricular shunts divert CSF in patients with hydrocephalus, often providing lifesaving intervention. Untreated shunt failure can lead to increased intracranial pressure and subsequent neurological injury. Phase-contrast MRI (PC-MRI) is a noninvasive technique to assess shunt function by measuring shunt flow. This work assists in clinical implementation of PC-MRI by quantifying and accounting for sources of variation in shunt flow measurements. Shunt phantoms were used to provide consistency between scanners, with flow rates spanning a physiological range. title: Disrupting SORL1-retromer endosomal recycling in mice drives the age-dependent neurodegenerative signature of Alzheimer's disease
summary: MRI studies have mapped the atrophic signature that distinguishes Alzheimer's disease (AD), isolating regions differentially vulnerable to its age-dependent neurodegenerative process. An endosomal recycling pathway regulated by the interaction of SORL1 with retromer is pathogenically disrupted in AD. Here we test the hypothesis, that the pathway might drive the neurodegenerative process, via multiple yearlong studies in over 140 wildtype and SORL1 deficient mice, modeling SORL1's causative mutations. title: Brain representations of visual short-term memories during healthy human aging: occipital decline and frontoparietal compensation
summary: Visual short-term memory declines steeply with age, but the link to neural representations of memory content remains unknown. We used fMRI decoding to relate remembered motion-direction representations in visual and frontoparietal cortex to age and performance, in 115 adults, aged 25-87, from the Cambridge Centre for Ageing and Neuroscience (Cam-CAN) cohort. Decoding was strongest in visual cortex, but also significant in frontoparietal regions, with different profiles.
